title: Bolognese Ragù

items: 1.5 lb ground beef (short rib or chuck, trimmed of fat)
¾ lb ground pork (italian sausage works fine too)
28 oz can of Italian plum tomatoes, hand crushed, with juice
1-½ lbs tagliateli or pappardelle, cooked and drained
Freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table

steps: Heat the olive oil and 6 Tbsp butter in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until translucent. Add the celery and carrot and cook for about 2 minutes.
Add the beef and pork, a large pinch of salt, and about 20 turns of finely ground pepper. Break up the meat and cook until it loses its pink color.
Add the milk and simmer gently, stirring frequently, until it evaporates. Stir in the nutmeg.
Add the wine and simmer until it evaporates. Stir in the tomatoes and their juices. Reduce the heat to maintain a very gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for at least 3 hours, stirring occasionally. Add ½ cup water as needed to prevent sticking. Let the added water cook off before serving.
Toss the hot pasta with 1–2 Tbsp butter and the ragù. Serve with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
sourceNote: Adapted from Marcella Hazan’s Classic Italian Cooking.
